tldr: Across 23 headlines, the dominant advertised story is India and China competing for BRICS leadership and global influence, while Western-aligned outlets frame the summit as a geopolitical contest; state-aligned outlets (RT, CGTN, Tehran Times) counter-frame it as Global South solidarity and the ascent of a multipolar order against outdated Western institutions.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to use threat-signaling language ('descend on India', 'high-stakes', 'escalating global tensions') and to name Iran's Pezeshkian alongside Putin and Xi — framing the summit as a convergence of adversarial powers rather than a multilateral forum, a sensational angle absent from all other outlets.

Only headline to brand the summit an outright 'success story' and a Modi 'diplomatic masterclass' — explicit nationalist boosterism that no other Indian or international outlet, including The Hindu and NDTV, replicates at the title layer.

Sole headline framing the summit as a potential Chinese advantage ('Advantage China?'), the only title to directly challenge India's host-nation narrative — a sceptical angle that wire service body text typically reserves for analysis sections but surfaces here at RSS level.

Only headline to position BRICS explicitly against 'Western sanctions, power politics' — reducing the summit to an anti-Western shield framework, a framing absent from all other outlets including CGTN and RT, which emphasise multilateralism or reform rather than direct confrontation.

bottom_line: The headline layer sells the 2026 BRICS summit as an India-China leadership contest under Western scrutiny, with Fox News uniquely weaponizing threat language, Tehran Times alone naming Western sanctions as the enemy, and state-aligned outlets counter-framing the story as Global South solidarity and institutional ascent.
